paragraphs: Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai. In Pesachim 8b: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai; in Bava Batra 10a: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai. A student of Rabbi Meir, for in Avot chapter 3 he says in Rabbi Meir’s name. In the Mishnah, Eruvin chapter 5, 58a, in Rabbi Meir’s name. In Vayikra Rabbah, beginning of chapter 17: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, in Rabbi Meir’s name. That matter in Yalkut Psalms, section 73, has “Rabbi Dostai in the name of Rabbi Yannai in the name of Rabbi Meir”; this is a scribal error. At the end of Gittin chapter 1, 14b, he and Rabbi Yose ben Kipper were sent to Nehardea. Rabbi Achai ben Yoshiyah (see his entry) told them to collect his debt there; see there, and Jerusalem Talmud, end of Gittin chapter 1, and chapter Haomer, 64a. At the end of chapter Hammapelet, his students asked Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, “Why does a man pursue a woman …?” This Yannai is not Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher, since his son Dostai is a Tanna. In Kiddushin chapter 1, 12a: “The Italian issar—Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, and Rabbi Oshaya estimated ….” However, the reading before us is “Rabbi Dostai and Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Oshaya”; it appears thus twice there. His reading requires examination, for Rabbi Oshaya was in Rabbi’s time, and Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, in Rabbi Meir’s days. Yet Rabbi Meir too was in Rabbi’s days (see his entry). At the end of Jerusalem Talmud, Demai, Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi and Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, disagree. In the name of Rabbi Eliezer: Tosefta Shabbat, end of chapter 15. His burial is in Akhbara; see Rabbi Yannai.
